methodologyNote: Many-to-one (inbound: arrive by target, latest possible departure). Transfer penalty 5 min per change (the low end of published interchange valuations, about 5-18 min; sensitivity at 1 and 10 min in the stress-test report). Isochrones clipped to coastline. Wirral (209 LSOAs, 320,204 people) is left out of the population in both eras, because no Birkenhead or Wallasey municipal timetables were found; The 1937 feed is built from every route page of the Liverpool Corporation Official Tram & Bus Guide No. 27 (December 1937): 48 tram and 37 bus routes, including the Ribble and Crosville services the guide prints, plus the urban railways from primary 1939 timetables (LMS electric lines to Southport, Ormskirk and Aintree, the Kirkby, Huyton, Allerton and Alexandra Dock suburban trains, the CLC to Hunt's Cross and Gateacre, the Overhead Railway and the Mersey Railway to James Street; 1939 stands in for 1937). Printed departures, early and late cars and journey minutes are used as printed; tram pages that give only service intervals are filled at those intervals (peak hours assumed 07:00-09:30 and 16:30-18:30, which the guide never defines). Routes whose pages print no minutes are timed from the printed routes on the same streets. Routes 13 and 43B print no times and are assumed to run at their parent route's interval. Trams follow the surveyed track, buses modern roads.

robustness.basis: 10 phase seeds each of a best case (peak intervals, estimates -15%, 200 m stops, Overhead Railway every 3 min) and a worst case (off-peak intervals, estimates +15%, 450 m stops, no assumed routes 13/43B, no company buses, peak window 30 min earlier, uncertain readings dropped, Overhead Railway through trains only)
